entities.summary: Capital of the Neo-Assyrian Empire at its zenith (c. 705–612 BCE), located on the eastern bank of the Tigris River in modern Mosul, Iraq. Under Sennacherib and Ashurbanipal, Nineveh was one of the largest and most magnificent cities in the ancient world, enclosed by a 12-kilometer wall with fifteen gates. Home to Ashurbanipal's library, the Palace Without Rival, and extensive irrigation works. Its dramatic fall in 612 BCE to a coalition of Babylonians and Medes became a symbol of divine judgment in the Hebrew Bible (Book of Nahum, Book of Jonah).
